Its voltage and the resistor voltage decrease, so the magnitudes of voltage and current fall exponentially towards zero.

focus: Pumped-storage power system / 抽水蓄能电力系统
text:
0 7 Discuss the use of a pumped storage system as part of a country’s electrical
power supply.
In your answer you should:
• describe the principles of operation of the pumped storage system
• explain why the pumped storage system is used
• state and explain the factors that determine the maximum power available from
the system.
[6 marks]
explanation: Water is stored in high and low reservoirs. When supply exceeds demand, a motor drives pumps to move water uphill. When demand is high, water flows down through turbines and generators to provide electricity. This lets base-load stations run continuously and stores their surplus energy; rapid start-up meets sudden demand and can reduce operating costs. The available power depends on the water flow and speed. For a water jet, P = ½ρπr²v³, where ρ is water density, r is the jet's effective radius and v is water speed. Greater reservoir height gives more gravitational energy per kilogram and can produce a higher speed. Turbine size limits the flow, and friction and resistive heating reduce useful electrical power.

text:
0 3 . 1 Figure 2 is a plot of the variation of average binding energy per nucleon with
nucleon number.
Figure 2
Compare the processes of nuclear fission and nuclear fusion in which energy is
released.
In your answer:
• describe the nuclear changes involved in fission and fusion
• describe how each process can begin
• explain why fission reactions are confined to one part of Figure 2 and
fusion reactions are confined to a different part of Figure 2.
[6 marks]
explanation: In fusion, two light nuclei combine into a heavier nucleus. High temperature gives them enough kinetic energy to overcome electrostatic repulsion and get close enough to fuse. Energy-releasing fusion occurs on the left of the binding-energy-per-nucleon peak, where combining light nuclei increases binding energy per nucleon. In fission, a heavy nucleus splits into two smaller nuclei, often after absorbing a thermal neutron and becoming unstable. Energy-releasing fission occurs on the right of the peak, where the products have greater binding energy per nucleon. In both cases the products have lower total rest mass and energy is released. Fission involves many nucleons, so it can release substantial energy even with a smaller increase per nucleon.

explanation: Water is stored in high and low reservoirs. When supply exceeds demand, a motor drives pumps to move water uphill. When demand is high, water flows down through turbines and generators to provide electricity. This lets base-load stations run continuously and stores their surplus energy; rapid start-up meets sudden demand and can reduce operating costs.
